title: Google Ads
hired_for: An owner hires the Google Ads expert to catch shoppers who are already searching for what the brand sells, at a cost the margin can carry, and to stop paying for searches, products and placements that never buy.

jobs.job: Stop paying for searches that never buy
jobs.why: Broad and automatic matching pulls in searches that have nothing to do with the product. Every month they are not blocked, the spend is simply lost.

watch.metric: spend on search terms with clicks and no purchase above the waste line, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $2,600 last month went to 140 terms with no sale, like 'free sock pattern'. After: blocked at the right level, waste under $500 a month.

jobs.job: Split brand searches from everything else so growth is judged honestly
jobs.why: People searching the brand name would mostly buy anyway. Mixed into cold campaigns, they make weak campaigns look strong.

watch.metric: non-brand return on ad spend with brand searches excluded, trailing 30 days

drives.metric: cost per new customer from Google

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Shopping shows 4.2x but 38% of its sales come from brand searches. After: brand excluded, non-brand shows 2.3x and gets judged on that.

jobs.job: Keep Merchant Center clean so products stay live
jobs.why: Disapproved products or a suspended account take Shopping to zero overnight. Most suspensions come from fixable page or policy gaps.

watch.metric: disapproved products and days each stayed down, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 46 products disapproved for missing shipping info, down 9 days on average. After: fixed within 48 hours, under 5 at any time.

jobs.job: Stop spending on products that are about to sell out
jobs.why: Shopping and Performance Max keep bidding on a product until it is gone. Top spenders going out of stock waste budget and reset learning.

watch.metric: Google spend on products with under 14 days of stock, trailing 7 days
watch.source: Google Ads product report and Shopify inventory

drives.metric: wasted spend and lost orders from stockouts

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $1,900 last week on 3 products with 5 days of stock. After: those products drop to low priority and budget moves to in-stock winners.

jobs.job: Make sure Google gets the real value of every order
jobs.why: Google bids on what it is told. Missing or fixed-value purchases make it chase the wrong shoppers and make every return number wrong.

watch.metric: share of store orders Google records with real order value, trailing 7 days

drives.metric: accuracy of Google's bidding, seen as non-brand return on ad spend

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Google records 64% of orders and 20% of those at a fixed $1. After: 95% of orders with real value and one primary purchase action.

jobs.job: Keep non-brand cost per purchase under break-even
jobs.why: Non-brand search is where new customers come from, and where money is easiest to lose. The limit must come from the store's own margin, not an industry number.

watch.metric: non-brand cost per purchase against break-even from margin, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: non-brand costs $44 per purchase against a $36 break-even. After: cuts before raises bring it to $33 in 3 weeks.

jobs.job: Find the cause of a drop before changing anything
jobs.why: When sales dip, the reflex is to change bids and budgets everywhere. That hides the real cause and can make things worse.

watch.metric: day on day cost per purchase of the top 5 campaigns against their 14 day range

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 30% drop led to 11 changes in 2 days and no clear cause. After: the drop traced to one feed error in an hour, 1 fix made.

jobs.job: Keep budgets paced for the month and sized for our stage
jobs.why: Too small a budget starves learning; too big wastes money. Raising fast and cutting slow is the costly habit.

watch.metric: month to date Google spend against plan, and budget against 3 to 4x order value a day for each campaign

drives.metric: month end gross profit after ad spend

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 campaigns run on $15 a day with a $70 average order. After: budgets in range and the month lands within 5% of plan.

jobs.job: Take back control of Performance Max
jobs.why: Performance Max hides where money goes and quietly takes credit for brand searches and returning buyers. Default settings let it spend on video, display and pages the owner never chose.

watch.metric: share of Performance Max spend with a visible search term, and share of its sales from brand searches, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Google Ads Performance Max search terms and insights

drives.metric: new customer return from Performance Max

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: brand not excluded, page expansion on, automatic assets on; 45% of its sales are brand searches. After: all 3 off, brand share under 10%.

jobs.job: Cut products that spend but do not sell, and push those that do
jobs.why: In Shopping, a few products take clicks with no sales while the best sellers are held back. Weekly pruning moves the money.

watch.metric: spend on products with 30 or more clicks and no purchase, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 22 products took $1,400 last month with 0 sales. After: excluded or bid down; that money goes to the top 10 sellers.

jobs.job: Turn off default settings that quietly waste spend
jobs.why: New campaigns come with search partners, display on search, broad location and auto-applied suggestions switched on. Each leaks a little money every day.

watch.metric: spend on search partners, display on search campaigns and auto-applied changes, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Google Ads settings and change history

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 11% of search spend runs on partner sites with 3% of sales. After: off on every search campaign, auto-apply off.

jobs.job: Check Google's numbers against what the store actually made
jobs.why: Google counts sales its own way. Scaling on Google's return alone can grow spend while real profit falls.

watch.metric: gap between Google-reported purchase value and store revenue from Google traffic, trailing 30 days

drives.metric: new customer revenue per ad dollar across all channels

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Google says 5.0x, store orders from Google say 2.9x. After: the gap is tracked monthly and scale calls use the store number.

jobs.job: Earn the right to add budget before adding it
jobs.why: Adding budget or a new campaign type before tracking, feed and brand split are right just scales the mistakes.

watch.metric: scaling checks passed out of 5 (tracking, feed, brand split, return at current budget, stock)
watch.source: Google Ads, Merchant Center and Shopify

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 of 5 checks pass and a 40% raise is planned. After: raise held until 5 of 5 pass, then added in steps.

jobs.job: Write product titles that lead with what people search
jobs.why: Shopping has no keywords; the title is how Google matches the product. A title that leads with the brand name or a cute name misses the searches that buy.

watch.metric: Shopping impressions and click rate per product after a title change, trailing 28 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 60% of titles start with the brand name. After: product type and top converting term first in 70 characters; clicks up 18% on changed titles.

jobs.job: Keep the product feed complete and true
jobs.why: Missing barcodes, wrong prices, stale stock or poor images cut how often products show and can trigger suspension.

watch.metric: share of products with feed errors or missing key attributes

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 30% of variants have no barcode and the feed updates once a day. After: under 5% missing, updates every 6 hours.

jobs.job: Keep past customers out of campaigns meant to find new ones
jobs.why: Cold campaigns that sell to past customers look good but add few new buyers. The owner pays new-customer prices for old customers.

watch.metric: share of conversions in prospecting campaigns from returning customers, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Google Ads new versus returning customer data and Shopify

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 33% of prospecting sales are returning buyers. After: customer list excluded, under 12%.

jobs.job: Grow search on terms that already sell
jobs.why: Proven buying terms deserve their own exact match ads and budget. Left inside broad or automatic campaigns they get starved or overpaid.

watch.metric: sales and impression share on the top 20 converting terms, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 'merino hiking socks' converts at 6% but shows in 40% of searches. After: own exact match group, 75% impression share at the same cost per sale.

jobs.job: Run Shopping in a way that fits our catalog size and margins
jobs.why: One Shopping campaign for 400 products with margins from 20% to 70% spends where it is easy, not where profit is.

watch.metric: Shopping return on ad spend by margin tier, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Google Ads with margin labels from the feed

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: one campaign, low-margin items take 50% of spend. After: margin labels in the feed and 3 tiers with their own targets.

jobs.job: Write search ads that lead with product, price or offer
jobs.why: Search ads sit next to rivals. The ad that names the product, price and answer to the main worry wins the click.

watch.metric: search ad click rate and conversion rate, trailing 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 of 9 headlines repeat the brand name, click rate 3.4%. After: product, price and returns in headlines, click rate 4.3%.

jobs.job: Use the right bidding setting for our stage, and move up only when ready
jobs.why: Setting a return target too early chokes sales. Staying on open bidding too long overpays. The move depends on weekly conversion volume.

watch.metric: conversions per campaign per week, and actual return against the target over 4 weeks

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a return target of 6x on a campaign with 8 sales a week, spend down 70%. After: target set at actual 3.5x, spend and sales back.

jobs.job: Defend the brand name cheaply when rivals bid on it
jobs.why: If rivals bid on the brand name, a small brand campaign keeps those buyers. If nobody does, the money is better spent elsewhere.

watch.metric: brand search impression share and brand cost per click, trailing 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: brand campaign on automatic bidding pays $1.40 a click with no rival present. After: manual bidding, $0.35 a click, 95% impression share.

jobs.job: Turn on the free Merchant Center extras
jobs.why: Free listings, seller ratings, promotions and remarketing cost nothing to turn on and add clicks and trust to every Shopping ad.

watch.metric: free listing clicks and add-ons live out of 4, trailing 28 days

drives.metric: Google revenue at no ad cost

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 of 4 add-ons on, free listings bring 300 clicks a month. After: all 4 on, 900 free clicks a month.

jobs.job: Give every campaign one job and a written reason
jobs.why: Many small overlapping campaigns split the data and confuse reporting. The owner cannot tell what each one is for or which to cut.

watch.metric: live campaigns with a written purpose, and campaigns under 15 conversions a month

drives.metric: stability of cost per purchase week to week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 17 campaigns, 9 with under 5 sales a month. After: 6 campaigns, each with one job on file.

jobs.job: Build remarketing lists big enough to use
jobs.why: Remarketing to a list too small to serve wastes setup time. Cart abandoners are the most valuable list and are often missing.

watch.metric: size of each remarketing list against Google's serving minimum

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no cart abandoner list; site visitor list at 600. After: cart abandoner list built from GA4, both lists above the minimum before launch.

jobs.job: Decide when YouTube or Demand Gen is worth adding
jobs.why: Video reaches new people but only pays once search and Shopping are right and there is creative and budget to test for weeks.

watch.metric: readiness checks passed, then cost per new customer on video against Meta, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Google Ads and Meta Ads Manager

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: YouTube spends $2,000 a month with no conversion tracking on video. After: paused until search and Shopping pass their checks.
